  • TL;DR: For a Node.js application with an Express delivery layer, define three allowed widths, generate them from the approved master, and return a manifest for the responsive source set.
  • This decision record uses 320, 640, and 1280 pixels as proposed widths.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Generate a fixed set of WebP derivatives from each approved product photo, and make the transformation recipe part of their stored identity. The deciding constraint is the number of objects a marketplace agrees to retain after background removal, including photos reused as blog covers.

TL;DR: For a Node.js application with an Express delivery layer, define three allowed widths, generate them from the approved master, and return a manifest for the responsive source set. Keep arbitrary dimensions out of the public transformation contract. Budget derivative storage, cache variants, and telemetry separately; each has a different retention decision.

This decision record uses 320, 640, and 1280 pixels as proposed widths. They are example policy values, not measured requirements. A marketplace should replace them after reviewing its product cards, detail pages, and cover layouts. WebP supports transparency, according to the MDN image format guide, so a transparent background-removal result can remain transparent in these derivatives. That format capability does not establish acceptable edge quality for a particular catalog.

The invariant is a bounded recipe: one approved master produces at most three published derivative objects for one active recipe revision. Background removal precedes this recipe. Derive each width from that master rather than resizing an already reduced output. The proposed encoder policy preserves aspect ratio and alpha, fixes its quality settings, and declines to enlarge a source smaller than the requested width. These are application requirements, not defaults attributed to an image library.

Industry observers note that for a sufficiently large master, the chosen policy creates three derivatives plus the master. Keeping an older recipe revision adds another three derivatives until that revision expires. If both the original upload and the approved background-removed master are retained, count both. A storage estimate that silently treats them as one object has already lost track of its unit.

It has been revealed that an image smaller than 1280 pixels exposes a useful boundary. Under this policy, the manifest contains only the widths actually generated; it never labels a smaller image as 1280 pixels wide. The delivery contract therefore promises up to three candidates. If the application requires exactly three, enforce a minimum master width at ingestion and report that requirement to the uploader. Do not hide enlargement inside a supposedly fixed recipe.

Industry observers note that the stored identity should include the approved master revision and the recipe revision. A replacement master or a changed encoding policy gets latest derivative identities. A page can then refer to a specific manifest without interpreting an old URL as a different image. This spends storage during revision overlap in exchange for a simpler relationship between a URL and its bytes.

Without an expiry decision for superseded revisions, a bounded width list still permits unbounded historical storage.

The relevant comparison is when the system commits to a derivative, not which image-processing package it imports. The following options describe application designs, with their corresponding obligations.

It has been revealed that the first option is the decision here. It commits storage before demand is known, but lets the application validate the entire candidate set before advertising it to a product page or a blog cover. Demand remains uncertain. The second can defer work and storage. It also requires a policy for simultaneous first requests and for a candidate that is not yet available.

Neither option makes an unused derivative free to keep. The proposed retention job starts from active master and recipe revisions, then identifies superseded objects after an explicitly chosen grace period. That period should cover the application's own page and cache lifetime policies. This is a deployment obligation: shortening retention without considering existing references can leave pages pointing to deleted images.

The Express layer should expose an application-owned contract and leave encoder selection behind it. The curl example below defines a proposed local interface; it is not an existing public API or a claim about a library's options. Implement its validation and generation behavior before using these requests. The fixture must be an approved, background-removed master at least 1280 pixels wide if all three candidates are expected.

In a recent development, the first request submits one master under an illustrative catalog identifier. The recipe name selects server-owned settings: WebP output, the three allowed widths, aspect-ratio preservation, alpha preservation, and no enlargement. Clients cannot add a fourth width by appending a request parameter. Bind this operation to the marketplace's authenticated upload workflow rather than making arbitrary public uploads part of image delivery.

In the proposed contract, the submission succeeds only after the generated candidates have passed validation and their manifest is available. The second request reads that manifest. Its candidate entries carry a URL, actual pixel width, actual pixel height, media type, and encoded byte count. Those are requirements for this application interface. No particular response schema is implied by curl itself.

Recent findings suggest that the page renderer constructs a width-descriptor source set from the returned URLs and actual widths, and supplies a sizes value that describes the rendered layout. Keep a fallback image URL as well. This is the integration point for the reader implementing responsive images in Node.js and Express: return verified candidates, then render the responsive markup from them. Blog covers and product cards may share bytes when their geometry and transformation policy agree. A cover needing a different crop requires a distinct recipe, which must enter the object count.

Publication follows validation.

It has been revealed that before publishing the manifest, decode each output and check its declared dimensions, format, and expected transparency behavior. Use fixture photos with fine edges and transparent margins to assess the background-removal result after encoding. A completed HTTP request alone is insufficient evidence of acceptable image content. For errors, return a bounded application error category and retain enough correlation data to investigate; do not publish a manifest containing candidates that failed validation.

Consider a planning example with 10,000 accepted masters per day. Assume the three encoded derivatives together occupy 240,000 bytes per master, and assume every day's derivatives remain active for 30 days. That is 72,000,000,000 bytes, or 72 GB in decimal units, of derivative payload. These inputs are hypothetical accounting assumptions, not WebP compression measurements. They exclude masters, historical revisions, metadata, replication, and cache copies. Measure encoded output from representative marketplace photos before turning the estimate into a capacity commitment. For example, a recipe experiment that retains a complete second set for the same 30 days would add another 72 GB under these assumptions. Calling that experiment temporary does not change its retained bytes; deleting its superseded outputs does. Record its expiry when the experiment begins, and keep its outputs out of the active manifest until they are approved.

Industry observers note that under a separate hypothetical policy of one 400-byte event per generated derivative, the same volume produces 12,000,000 bytes of event payload daily. Seven days retain 84,000,000 bytes, or 84 MB in decimal units, before indexing or replication. Changing the image retention policy does not change that telemetry budget. Keeping request logs indefinitely would be a separate decision with a separate growth curve.

In a recent development, metric labels deserve the same discipline. Three width values crossed with two outcome values create six possible combinations before adding any other dimensions. Identifiers change that. Adding a photo identifier creates a series space that grows with the catalog. The proposed metric design therefore uses bounded width and outcome labels; photo identifiers belong in selectively retained diagnostic records. Recipe revisions also need a retirement policy if they are used as labels.

According to recent reports, sampling is a trade-off. Counting every generation outcome supports an aggregate failure rate, while retaining only a sample of successful diagnostic events reduces the detail available for reconstructing an individual success. Keep validation-failure diagnostics under a separate, bounded policy, and document the success-sampling probability. A sample cannot promise a complete history of every photo. If that history is required, give it an explicit retention budget instead of treating sampled logs as an audit ledger.

Recent findings suggest that the acceptance test should include a replacement master and a recipe revision, not just three successful output files. Verify that previous pages retain their intended candidates during the overlap period and that retired revisions become eligible for deletion afterward. Review actual derivative bytes, retained revisions, and diagnostic volume together after deployment, because an encoder change that reduces individual file sizes can still increase the retained total if it adds a second recipe whose outputs remain available beside the first set for the full retention period.

Arbitrary dimensions are rejected for this catalog delivery path because they remove the fixed upper bound on derivative variants. A seller-facing crop editor is a valid separate use case: exploratory dimensions can be useful before approval. Give those previews a quota and expiry, then submit only the approved master to the published recipe.

In a recent development, the decision holds while the marketplace can describe its published layouts with a small candidate set. Revisit the widths when layout evidence changes. Keep the governing rule: every retained image, cache variant, and diagnostic record needs an identity and a lifetime that someone can explain.

According to recent reports, what's your FI number? Calculate it in 60 seconds.

The one number that changes everything.

Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.

A primary beneficiary is the person or entity you designate to receive an asset — such as a life insurance policy, 401(k), IRA, or bank account — when you die. If you name multiple primary beneficiaries, they split the asset according to the percentages you specify. A contingent beneficiary (also called a secondary or backup beneficiary) receives the asset only if all primary beneficiaries are unable to inherit, either because they predeceased you, disclaimed the inheritance, or cannot be located.

Industry observers note that this layered system exists because life is unpredictable. If you name your spouse as primary beneficiary on your life insurance and you both die in the same accident, the contingent beneficiary ensures the proceeds go where you intended rather than into your general estate where they become subject to probate.

Recent findings suggest that you can name individuals, trusts, charities, or even your estate as a beneficiary. However, naming your estate is generally a poor choice because it forces the asset through probate, exposing it to creditors, delays, and court costs. The entire purpose of a beneficiary designation is to transfer assets outside of probate — naming your estate defeats that advantage.

In a recent development, when naming multiple beneficiaries, you must choose a distribution method that determines what happens if one beneficiary dies before you. This choice is critical and frequently misunderstood.

Industry observers note that per stirpes (Latin for "by the branch") means each branch of your family tree receives its designated share. If your son predeceases you, his share passes down to his children (your grandchildren) in equal portions. The family branch stays intact.

Per capita (Latin for "by the head") means assets are divided equally among surviving beneficiaries only. If your son predeceases you, his share is redistributed among your other surviving beneficiaries — his children receive nothing.

For most families, per stirpes is the safer default because it prevents accidental disinheritance of grandchildren. If you want surviving beneficiaries to absorb the shares of those who predecease you, per capita achieves that — but make sure that outcome aligns with your actual wishes.

Some financial institutions also offer per capita at each generation, which distributes equally among the nearest living generation first, then passes remaining shares equally to the next generation. This hybrid approach is less common but available at some custodians.

Beneficiary designations are deceptively simple forms that create binding legal consequences. The most expensive mistakes happen not from malice but from neglect.

In most states, a divorce does not automatically remove your ex-spouse from beneficiary designations on retirement accounts or life insurance policies. Federal law (ERISA) governs employer-sponsored aims like 401(k)s, and ERISA does not recognize state divorce revocation statutes. If you divorce and never enhancement your 401(k) beneficiary, your ex-spouse can legally claim the entire balance — even if your will leaves everything to your fresh spouse.

Minor children cannot legally receive life insurance proceeds or retirement account distributions. If you name a 5-year-old as beneficiary, the insurance company will not release funds until a court appoints a guardian or conservator of the child's property. This process costs $2,000 to $5,000 in legal fees, takes months, and requires ongoing court reporting. Instead, name a trust for the benefit of the child or use your state's Uniform Transfers to Minors Act (UTMA) custodial designation.

If you leave the beneficiary field blank or all named beneficiaries predecease you without a contingent, the asset typically defaults to your estate. This triggers probate, adds 6 to 18 months of delay, and exposes the asset to estate creditors. Always name at least one contingent beneficiary.

Your beneficiary designations and your will can contradict each other. The beneficiary designation always wins. If your will indicates your daughter gets your IRA but the IRA beneficiary form still names your brother, your brother gets the IRA. Review both documents together annually.

Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.

Set a recurring calendar reminder to review every beneficiary designation once per year — ideally alongside your tax preparation. Pull statements from your 401(k), IRA, life insurance, bank accounts, and brokerage accounts. Verify that primary and contingent designations match your current wishes. This 30-minute annual review prevents the kind of outdated-beneficiary disasters that lead to costly litigation and assets going to unintended recipients.

Recent findings suggest that yes. You can name multiple primary beneficiaries and assign a percentage to each. For example, you could name three children as primary beneficiaries at 33.3% each. The percentages must total 100%.

If all primary beneficiaries predecease you and no contingent is named, the asset typically defaults to your estate. This forces the asset through probate, where it is subject to creditor claims, court costs, and delays of 6 to 18 months.

For state-law-governed accounts like IRAs and life insurance, some states have revocation-upon-divorce statutes — but not all. For ERISA-governed accounts like employer 401(k)s, federal law does not recognize state divorce revocation. You must manually update the beneficiary form after divorce to be safe.

In a recent development, yes. A beneficiary can file a qualified disclaimer within 9 months of the account holder's death. The disclaimed asset then passes to the contingent beneficiary or according to the proposal's default rules. Disclaimers are sometimes used for tax planning purposes.

Naming a trust provides control over how and when assets are distributed — especially useful for minor children, spendthrift beneficiaries, or blended families. However, trusts named as IRA beneficiaries must meet specific IRS requirements to qualify for stretch distributions under the SECURE Act. Consult an estate planning attorney before naming a trust as retirement account beneficiary.

Sources indicate that A POD designation on a bank account functions exactly like a beneficiary designation. The named person receives the account balance upon your death without going through probate. You maintain full control of the account during your lifetime and can change the POD beneficiary at any time.

Primary and contingent beneficiary designations are among the most powerful — and most overlooked — estate planning tools. They transfer assets instantly upon death, bypass probate entirely, and override your will in every state. The 30 minutes it takes to review and revision your designations after every major life event can save your family months of legal proceedings, thousands in attorney fees, and the heartbreak of assets going to unintended recipients.

Restate deployment registration puts network reachability inside the invocation path

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (456 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dev

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Restate is a durable execution service that proxies calls to registered service endpoints.
  • The security model therefore crosses two networks.
  • According to recent reports, the count-only query (title="Restate" || http.body="restate.dev" || app="Restate") returned 87 matches on 2026-11-24T21:49:37.422258Z.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Restate is a durable execution service that proxies calls to registered service endpoints. The service process contains handlers and workflow logic. Registration tells Restate where to find those handlers and lets the server route invocations to them.

The security model therefore crosses two networks. Clients and workflows call Restate, and Restate calls the registered service endpoint. A deployment URL that is reachable from the cluster may be acceptable for one trust zone and dangerous for another. An endpoint that accepts arbitrary registration can become a path to internal services.

According to recent reports, the count-only query (title="Restate" || http.body="restate.dev" || app="Restate") returned 87 matches on 2026-11-24T21:49:37.422258Z. The refined query uses restate.dev to reduce matches against the ordinary word. It can include documentation, examples and hosted pages.

It has been revealed that inventory registered deployments, their URLs and the service schemas they expose. Review who can call the admin API and change a deployment address. Separate the ingress API used by clients from the admin API used by operators.

The Restate operator documentation describes network peer settings for ingress, admin and node ports. Use those controls to limit which pods, services or namespaces can reach each plane. A shared service network that reaches the admin API without policy expands the consequence of a compromised workload.

It has been revealed that review service endpoint authentication and egress policy. Restate proxies calls, but the target endpoint still needs to reject requests it should not accept. Use private addresses and service identities where possible.

According to recent reports, register a test handler in a non-production namespace. Attempt to invoke it from an unapproved client and from an approved ingress gateway. Confirm that the admin API rejects a deployment registration from a namespace that should not control routing.

Review Restate logs and audit records for deployment registration, endpoint updates and unusual invocation destinations. Correlate them with Kubernetes network policy and service-account activity. A deployment URL change is a routing change even when the service code remains the same.

If an unexpected endpoint was registered, remove it through the supported admin workflow and preserve its schema and invocation records. Rotate credentials available to the endpoint and review target-service logs for calls that began during the exposure. Check whether the endpoint could reach metadata or internal control APIs.

Keep admin and ingress ports on separate network paths. Restrict deployment registration to approved identities. Use explicit network peers and least-privilege service accounts. Monitor registration changes as configuration, not routine application traffic.

The count does not prove that a Restate admin API is exposed or that arbitrary registrations are allowed. It identifies a population for owner verification. The relevant evidence is the effective listener, authentication, network policy and registered endpoint list.

    Making an Arduino ultrasonic box sorter more reliable: the code mitigations and why they exist

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (538 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dev

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • I built this Arduino conveyor sorter to classify boxes by height, and most of the less obvious parts of the code are there to solve problems I ran into while building it.
    • Code and documentation: https://github.com/mosalah34/box-sorter-arduino.
    • Recent findings suggest that the sketch drives a belt motor through a driver with direction inputs (IN1, IN2) and an enable/PWM input (ENA) at fixed speed 80 of 255.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    I built this Arduino conveyor sorter to classify boxes by height, and most of the less obvious parts of the code are there to solve problems I ran into while building it. This post walks through each mitigation, what it addresses, and the published background behind it.

    Code and documentation: https://github.com/mosalah34/box-sorter-arduino.

    Recent findings suggest that the sketch drives a belt motor through a driver with direction inputs (IN1, IN2) and an enable/PWM input (ENA) at fixed speed 80 of 255. Two ultrasonic trigger/echo sensors watch for a box: one above the belt, one at the side. A servo on pin 9 moves a gate between 0 and 160 degrees. A 16x2 I2C LCD at address 0x27 demonstrates status. The sketch does not fix specific part models, so any model named below is a common choice that fits these interfaces. A published example of the same pattern, with an Arduino Uno, an HC-SR04, a servo and an I2C LCD, is the IEOM 2024 paper "Automatic Product Counting & Sorting by Conveyor Belt" (https://ieomsociety.org/proceedings/bangladesh2024/217.pdf).

    In a recent development, sources note that HC-SR04 modules return missing or wildly wrong readings: soft or angled surfaces lose the echo, and random large values appear from earlier pings or far walls. UMass's Physical Computing Makerspace page recommends waiting 60 ms or more between pings and using a median of five readings (https://make.cs.umass.edu/uc/ultrasonic.html). An Arduino Forum thread on 2000 cm+ outliers also points to a median filter (https://forum.arduino.cc/t/how-do-i-remove-outliers-in-the-data-provided-by-the-hc-sr04-ultrasonic-sensor/1279240/2).

    According to recent reports, in the sketch: readDistance uses a 25 ms echo timeout and returns 0 for anything under 2 cm or over 200 cm. The measurement takes 5 top readings 100 ms apart, sorts them, takes the median, drops readings more than 0.35 cm from it, and requires at least 4 accepted. Otherwise it demonstrates "Unstable Read" and moves on instead of guessing.

    One bad echo should not stop a belt. The sketch requires both sensors to see a change: the top sensor 0.8 cm closer than the 7.0 cm empty value, and the side sensor 0.8 cm closer than a median baseline taken at startup. It needs 2 confirmations in a row. If the side baseline cannot be read (fewer than 5 valid out of 9), it stops with an error instead of running uncalibrated.

    Recent findings suggest that A box measured while the belt moves gives unstable values. The sketch stops the motor, waits 250 ms, then measures. After classification it waits for both sensors to read empty again before accepting the next box, which prevents one box being counted twice.

    According to recent reports, distances near a threshold flip between classes. The sketch uses a dead band: 3.4 cm or less is large, 3.6 cm or more is small, and the range between is not classified as either. A caution on the display: the "Height" shown is the sensor-to-box-top distance. Real box height is the sensor's mounting height above the belt minus that reading.

    These are common failures reported in guides, not claims about this build.

    This post does not report measured accuracy, throughput, or hardware validation. The thresholds (3.4 / 3.6 / 7.0 cm) are values in the sketch and would need calibration for any physical setup.

    It has been revealed that SEMrush and Ahrefs are among the most popular tools in the SEO industry. Both companies have been in business for years and have thousands of customers per month. If you're a professional SEO or trying to do digital marketing on your own, at some point you'll likely consider using a tool to help with your efforts. Ahrefs and SEMrush are two names that will likely appear on your shortlist. In this guide, I'm going to help you learn more about these SEO tools and how to choose the one that's best for your purposes.What is SEMrush? SEMrush is a popular SEO tool with a wide range of features—it's the leading competitor research service for online marketers. SEMrush's SEO Keyword Magic tool offers over 20 billion Google-approved keywords, which are constantly updated and it's the largest keyword database. The program was developed in 2007 as SeoQuake is a small Firefox extension Features Most accurate keyword data: Accurate keyword search volume data is crucial for SEO and PPC campaigns by allowing you to identify what keywords are most likely to bring in big sales from ad clicks. SEMrush constantly updates its databases and provides the most accurate data.Largest Keyword database: SEMrush's Keyword Magic Tool now features 20-billion keywords, providing marketers and SEO professionals the largest database of keywords. All SEMrush people receive daily ranking data, mobile volume information, and the option to buy additional keywords by default with no additional payment or add-ons neededMost accurate position tracking tool: This tool provides all subscribers with basic tracking capabilities, making it suitable for SEO professionals. Plus, the Position Tracking tool provides local-level data to everyone who uses the tool.SEO Data Management: SEMrush makes managing your online data easy by allowing you to create visually appealing custom PDF reports, including Branded and White Label reports, report scheduling, and integration with GA, GMB, and GSC.Toxic link monitoring and penalty recovery: With SEMrush, you can make a detailed analysis of toxic backlinks, toxic scores, toxic markers, and outreach to those sites.Content Optimization and Creation Tools: SEMrush offers content optimization and creation tools that let you create SEO-friendly content. Some features include the SEO Writing Assistant, On-Page SEO Check, er/SEO Content Template, Content Audit, Post Tracking, Brand Monitoring. Ahrefs Ahrefs is a leading SEO platform that offers a set of tools to grow your search traffic, research your competitors, and monitor your niche. The firm was founded in 2010, and it has become a popular choice among SEO tools. Ahrefs has a keyword index of over 10.3 billion keywords and offers accurate and extensive backlink data updated every 15-30 minutes and it is the world's most extensive backlink index database. Features Backlink alerts data and new keywords: Get an alert when your site is linked to or discussed in blogs, forums, comments, or when new keywords are added to a blog posting about you.Intuitive interface: The intuitive design of the widget helps you see the overall health of your website and search engine ranking at a glance.Site Explorer: The Site Explorer will give you an in-depth look at your site's search traffic.Domain ComparisonReports with charts and graphsJavaScript rendering and a site audit can identify SEO problems.A question explorer that provides well-crafted topic suggestions Direct Comparisons: Ahrefs vs SEMrush Now that you know a little more about each tool, let's take a look at how they compare. I'll analyze each tool to see how they differ in interfaces, keyword research resources, rank tracking, and competitor analysis. User Interface Ahrefs and SEMrush both offer comprehensive information and quick metrics regarding your website's SEO performance. However, Ahrefs takes a bit more of a hands-on approach to getting your account fully set up, whereas SEMrush's simpler dashboard can give you access to the data you need swiftly. In this section, we provide a brief overview of the elements found on each dashboard and highlight the ease with which you can complete tasks. AHREFS The Ahrefs dashboard is less cluttered than that of SEMrush, and its primary menu is at the very top of the page, with a search bar designed only for entering URLs. Additional features of the Ahrefs platform include: You can see analytics from the dashboard, including search engine rankings to domain ratings, referring domains, and backlinkJumping from one tool to another is easy. You can use the Keyword Explorer to find a keyword to target and then directly track your ranking with one click.The website offers a tooltip helper tool that allows you to hover your mouse over something that isn't clear and get an in-depth explanation. SEMRUSH When you log into the SEMrush Tool, you will find four main modules. These include information about your domains, organic keyword analysis, ad keyword, and site traffic. You'll also find some other options like A search bar allows you to enter a domain, keyword, or anything else you wish to explore.A menu on the left side of the page provides quick links to relevant information, including marketing insights, projects, keyword analytics, and more.The customer support resources located directly within the dashboard can be used to communicate with the support team or to learn about other resources such as webinars and blogs.Detailed descriptions of every resource offered. This detail is beneficial for new marketers, who are just starting. WHO WINS? Both Ahrefs and SEMrush have user-friendly dashboards, but Ahrefs is less cluttered and easier to navigate. On the other hand, SEMrush offers dozens of extra tools, including access to customer support resources. When deciding on which dashboard to use, consider what you value in the user interface, and test out both. Rank Tracking If you're looking to track your website's search engine ranking, rank tracking features can help. You can also use them to monitor your competitors. Let's take a look at Ahrefs vs. SEMrush to see which tool does a better job. Ahrefs The Ahrefs Rank Tracker is simpler to use. Just type in the domain name and keywords you want to analyze, and it spits out a report showing you the search engine results page (SERP) ranking for each keyword you enter. Rank Tracker looks at the ranking performance of keywords and compares them with the top rankings for those keywords. Ahrefs also offers: You'll see metrics that help you understand your visibility, traffic, average position, and keyword difficulty. It gives you an idea of whether a keyword would be profitable to target or not. SEMRUSH SEMRush offers a tool called Position Tracking. This tool is a project tool—you must set it up as a new project. Below are a few of the most popular features of the SEMrush Position Tracking tool: All subscribers are given regular data updates and mobile search rankings upon subscribing The platform provides opportunities to track several SERP features, including Local tracking. Intuitive reports allow you to track statistics for the pages on your website, as well as the keywords used in those pages. Identify pages that may be competing with each other using the Cannibalization report. WHO WINS? Ahrefs is a more user-friendly option. It takes seconds to enter a domain name and keywords. From there, you can quickly decide whether to proceed with that keyword or figure out how to rank better for other keywords. SEMrush allows you to check your mobile rankings and ranking updates daily, which is something Ahrefs does not offer. SEMrush also offers social media rankings, a tool you won't find within the Ahrefs platform. Both are good which one do you like let me know in the comment. Keyword Research Keyword research is closely related to rank tracking, but it's used for deciding which keywords you proposal on using for future content rather than those you use now. When it comes to SEO, keyword research is the most important thing to consider when comparing the two platforms. AHREFS The Ahrefs Keyword Explorer provides you with thousands of keyword ideas and filters search results based on the chosen search engine. Ahrefs supports several features, including: It can search multiple keywords in a single search and analyze them together. At SEMrush, you also have this feature in Keyword Overview.Ahrefs has a variety of keywords for different search engines, including Google, YouTube, Amazon, Bing, Yahoo, Yandex, and other search engines.When you click on a keyword, you can see its search volume and keyword difficulty, but also other keywords related to it, which you didn't use. SEMRUSH SEMrush's Keyword Magic Tool has over 20 billion keywords for Google. You can type in any keyword you want, and a list of suggested keywords will appear. The Keyword Magic Tool also lets you to: Show performance metrics by keywordSearch results are based on both broad and exact keyword matches.Show data like search volume, trends, keyword difficulty, and CPC.Show the first 100 Google search results for any keyword.Identify SERP Features and Questions related to each keywordSEMrush has released a new Keyword Gap Tool that uncovers potentially useful keyword opportunities for you, including both paid and organic keywords. WHO WINS? Both of these tools offer keyword research features and allow users to break down complicated tasks into something that can be understood by beginners and advanced users alike. If you're interested in keyword suggestions, SEMrush appears to have more keyword suggestions than Ahrefs does. It also continues to add new features, like the Keyword Gap tool and SERP Questions recommendations. Competitor Analysis Both platforms offer competitor analysis tools, eliminating the need to come up with keywords off the top of your head. Each tool is useful for finding keywords that will be useful for your competition so you know they will be valuable to you. AHREFS Ahrefs' domain comparison tool lets you compare up to five websites (your website and four competitors) side-by-side.it also shows you how your site is ranked against others with metrics such as backlinks, domain ratings, and more. Use the Competing Domains section to see a list of your most direct competitors, and explore how many keywords matches your competitors have. To find more information about your competitor, you can look at the Site Explorer and Content Explorer tools and type in their URL instead of yours. SEMRUSH SEMrush provides a variety of insights into your competitors' marketing tactics. The platform enables you to research your competitors effectively. It also offers several resources for competitor analysis including: Traffic Analytics helps you identify where your audience comes from, how they engage with your site, what devices visitors use to view your site, and how your audiences overlap with other websites. SEMrush's Organic Research examines your website's major competitors and shows their organic search rankings, keywords they are ranking for, and even if they are ranking for any (SERP) features and more. The Market Explorer search field allows you to type in a domain and lists websites or articles similar to what you entered. Market Explorer also allows users to perform in-depth data analytics on These companies and markets. WHO WINS? SEMrush wins here because it has more tools dedicated to competitor analysis than Ahrefs. However, Ahrefs offers a lot of functionality in this area, too. It takes a combination of both tools to gain an advantage over your competition.     A three-field key built from the user agent stops routine auto-updates from reading as fresh devices — and the version string is the field you have to throw away.

    In a recent development, caution — use it at your own risk. A user agent is user-controlled text. This is a coarse, spoofable hint for analytics and benign personalization, not authentication, fraud prevention, or a unique-person identifier. Track people only with informed consent, check the privacy rules that apply to you (including ePrivacy/GDPR and CCPA-style laws), and treat every fingerprint as an approximation. If you ship it, the consequences are yours.

    Your sign-in handler is short, readable, and wrong in a way that only highlights up after a patch Tuesday.

    Most days this works. Then Chrome moves from 120.0.0.0 to 121.0.0.0 in the background, and the same laptop on the same network produces a fresh string:.

    One patch release becomes a support ticket. A macOS point release does the same thing. A browser that changes its UA format does it to everyone at once.

    Three fixes come to mind, and each one moves the problem.

    You need one key that stays the same through routine updates and still differs when the browser or platform actually changes, and every string-level trick either keeps the noise or throws away the signal.

    The shape of the fix is to let a parser split the string, then build the key from only the parts that identify a class of device:.

    deviceFingerprint is a thin wrapper that returns just .fingerprint for callers that do not need the display fields.

    Think of a library card stamped with the branch, the section, and the format — never the checkout date.

    It has been revealed that two consequences. First, two people with the same card look identical; that is the cost of a stable class. Second, the version is not lost — it is still on the parsed object if you need it for display, but it stays out of the key.

    The checkout date tells you when; the stamps tell you who.

    Install the parser and a test runner, then copy these two files:.

    Imports below use @/, which maps to src/. Swap in whatever alias your project uses, or use relative paths the way the test file does.

    src/utils/device-fingerprint.ts — the whole utility:.

    src/utils/device-fingerprint.test.ts — the contract, pinned so a dependency bump cannot quietly change your keys:.

    It has been revealed that this is written against ua-parser-js 2.x (^2.0.10) and Vitest. The parser ships lookup tables, so pin the major version and re-run this test file when you bump it; a newly introduced detection rule can change a name and therefore your key.

    Your buckets are Chrome|Windows|unknown instead of a long tail of patch versions, so a graph of "devices this week" does not spike every time a browser auto-updates.

    Recent findings suggest that the comparison uses the stable key, while the email uses the friendly fields from the same parse. Chrome 120 to 121 is silent; a switch from Windows Chrome to macOS Safari is not.

    Every optional field is normalized to null, so a missing device type never leaks the literal string "undefined" into a log or a UI.

    When a parser upgrade changes a detection rule, this test fails before your analytics buckets split in production.

    Industry observers note that ❌ Do not use deviceFingerprint as a session id, an auth factor, or a unique-visitor counter. Two people on Chrome and Windows get the same value, and one person can change their user agent in a single request.

    Sources indicate that read the caution at the top before you ship this. Reach for it only when all three are true:.

    The smell test: if two different people with the same laptop setup would break your feature, this utility is the wrong tool.

    Recent findings suggest that parsing is delegated, not hand-rolled. UAParser(userAgent) returns { browser, os, device }. Writing your own regex puts you in the business of tracking every vendor's UA format; the library owns that table. The cost is a dependency and its parse tables at module load.

    Recent findings suggest that missing fields become null, not undefined. browser.name ?? null, os.name ?? null, and device.type ?? null give callers one predictable empty value. That matters when the result crosses a serialization boundary: JSON.stringify drops undefined properties but keeps null ones, so the shape stays identical.

    Sources indicate that the key is three fields joined by |. Versions are deliberately absent. The unknown sentinel keeps the arity: a Windows Chrome desktop is Chrome|Windows|unknown, never the shorter Chrome|Windows, so a later device-type detection cannot silently reshuffle your buckets. The separator is for humans reading logs, not for security.

    Industry observers note that deviceFingerprint is a one-line wrapper. Callers that only need the key can import one function; callers that need the label use parseUserAgent. Both paths run the same parse, so they cannot disagree.

    Industry observers note that the cost is one parse and a few strings per call. There is no cache, no timer, and no retained reference: the UA string is borrowed for the call, three fields are normalized, and one joined string is allocated. Call it once per request or render and pass the result around instead of re-parsing in a loop.

    Sources indicate that the discarded render is the reason this is a pure function: a render that is thrown away computes a string nobody uses, and a committed render computes the same string again. No effect, no cleanup, no ordering bug.

    Server-rendering note. On the server the string comes from the {% raw %}user-agent header; in the browser it comes from navigator.userAgent. Those are not guaranteed to match. Chromium's User-Agent Reduction freezes much of the version detail and moves it to Client Hints, so a client-side parse can return unknown where a server-side header still has detail, and mobile detection can vary. Pick one side as the source of truth for your keys and use it consistently.

    It has been revealed that compared to built-ins. navigator.userAgentData (Client Hints) gives structured brands, platform, and mobile fields, but it is Chromium-only, needs a secure context, and server access requires an Accept-CH opt-in. It also carries version detail that this utility intentionally discards, so it does not buy stability for this use case. No built-in gives a stable, cross-browser device-class string; the library is doing the normalization work, and the three-field key is what makes the result boring enough to store.

    In a recent development, the trade is stability bought by throwing information away. You give up versions and uniqueness, and in return a routine revision stops looking like a new device.

    According to recent reports, this belongs in coarse analytics and benign personalization. When you need to know who is at the door, the boring answer — a consented first-party id or a real session — wins every time. And use this at your own risk: it is a hint, not an identity.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, TL;DR: For a production Node.js customer support agent, use a NestJS exception filter for HTTP failures, an interceptor for request timing, and explicit wrappers for cron jobs and workers. Add process-level handlers as a final failure boundary. Keep latency and cost observations separate from exception counts. A rejected request, a failed agent step, and a process crash need different responses.

    Start with signal quality. If one failed support-agent step produces three identical reports, the dashboard gets louder without explaining more. If a scheduled job never starts, exception capture alone cannot tell you it is missing.

    Industry observers note that before: every catch block writes a stack trace, the interceptor writes another, and the HTTP filter writes a third. A support request looks like several incidents. Meanwhile, a worker outside the HTTP pipeline can fail without reaching any of those handlers.

    After, in words: HTTP request → timing interceptor → support loop → exception filter on failure. Separately: scheduler or worker → observed task wrapper → original caller receives the rejection. Process handlers sit outside both paths.

    It has been revealed that use the filter to classify HTTP exceptions. An expected client rejection should retain its HTTP status without automatically becoming an incident. Use the interceptor to measure the whole request, including failed requests. Wrap the scheduled or queued operation itself because an HTTP interceptor does not surround background execution. A process handler is the last chance to report an otherwise unhandled failure; it cannot replace the wrapper that knows which task was running.

    For the support loop, attach a stable operation name such as support.agent or support.followup. Keep ticket identifiers and customer messages out of metric labels. Prometheus's instrumentation guidance explains why unbounded label values create cardinality problems. A useful duration series can become an expensive collection of almost unique series if every support ticket becomes a label value.

    There is a second trap: adding together elapsed times from parallel agent steps overstates wall-clock latency. Measure the enclosing operation with a monotonic clock. Sum actual per-call cost observations separately, including paid retries where applicable. Neither the number of exceptions nor the duration of a request tells you its bill.

    This is an instrumentation harness with an authenticated discovery check, not a model client. It starts a NestJS HTTP probe and runs two deliberate background failure fixtures. Replace the fixture callbacks with the existing cron and worker entry points. Their rejected promises remain visible to the caller.

    Sources indicate that use a Node.js project with TypeScript and install @nestjs/common, @nestjs/core, @nestjs/platform-express, reflect-metadata, rxjs, and tsx. Set INFRAI_API_KEY and INFRAI_API_ORIGIN to your key and the documented HTTPS API origin, without a version suffix. The startup check reads the public discovery manifest; it does not export captured errors. Save this as telemetry.ts and run it with npx tsx telemetry.ts. The example applies Nest decorators as functions so it does not require a decorator compiler configuration.

    Open http://localhost:3000/support/probe for the HTTP timing observation. At startup, each background fixture emits an exception observation and a duration observation. The final catch belongs to the demonstration harness. In a real worker, let the queue integration receive the rejection so its failure policy can act; swallowing it can turn failed work into an apparent success.

    Industry observers note that the discovery check makes at most 3 attempts with a 10000 ms timeout per attempt. Discovery is a read-only GET, so its bounded retries cannot duplicate a write. The check honors Retry-After on a rate-limit response and surfaces other HTTP errors. It verifies connectivity to the manifest, not authenticated capture delivery. The reporting boundary remains local JSON output until a schema-checked capture adapter replaces it.

    The optional cost environment variable accepts an actual observed call cost. It supplies no default and performs no billing lookup. Connect recordCallCost at each real backend call's completion, with the amount that call reports. When aggregating these events, preserve enough correlation to associate calls with one agent run, and prevent collector redelivery from counting a call twice. Do not use a ticket identifier as a metric label to achieve that correlation.

    The output deliberately excludes messages, stacks, and request bodies. Support tickets can contain sensitive text, and exception messages can repeat it. A production capture adapter should add reviewed diagnostic fields after redaction. The example is a narrow, copyable boundary demonstration; it does not implement a durable telemetry exporter. In particular, process.exit does not wait for buffered output. Choose a bounded flush and termination policy for the actual reporter, and use a supervisor to restart the process rather than continuing after an uncaught exception.

    According to recent reports, error capture, metrics, and missing-run detection produce different signals. Evaluate them with the same support-agent scenario: an HTTP rejection, a failed follow-up worker, a scheduled task that never starts, and an expensive successful loop. This is a proposed acceptance exercise, not a benchmark result.

    Recent findings suggest that the shared interface is plain HTTP: no SDK to install. Its self-describing API provides public discovery with JSON Schema and runnable examples in 10 languages. That helps verify a worker's capture adapter without importing another client library. The broader surface covers 295 routes across 20 modules, so related storage and scheduling calls can use the same conventions. This is useful breadth, not evidence of deeper incident investigation.

    The trade-off is operational scope. A capture-and-query workflow is not suitable as the sole monitor for missing scheduled executions. Choose Healthchecks for that signal. For aggregate latency, choose Prometheus and evaluate Grafana for its presentation; for exception investigation, evaluate Sentry. They are not interchangeable replacements. A team can reasonably combine exception tracking with metrics and heartbeat monitoring because the questions differ.

    Keep the choice testable. If the pain is a missing nightly follow-up, validate heartbeat delivery first. If successful agent loops are getting slower, inspect duration distributions and call-level accounting before increasing exception volume. If the pain is repeated credentials and fragmented backend accounting, integration consolidation deserves weight alongside investigation depth.

    Industry observers note that filtering expected client rejections out of incident capture does not require discarding their counts. Keep aggregate status observations if they help explain the support workflow. Raise the signal when an allegedly expected rejection suddenly dominates traffic, but keep that policy separate from reporting every instance as an application defect.

    Recent findings suggest that also distinguish duplicate reporting from repeated execution. The same thrown error reported by an interceptor and a filter is usually one failure observed twice. A worker retry is another execution attempt, with its own latency and potentially its own cost. Record attempt context in diagnostic events, while keeping metric labels bounded. That distinction matters when a support agent repeatedly retries a tool call before finally returning a successful answer.

    Exception groups alone cannot establish distributed causality. Correlation identifiers help connect records; they do not create a span tree. Use a tracing system when the question requires parent-child timing across services, and use symbolication or replay tooling only when those investigation needs actually exist.

    Finally, no exception appears when a cron job simply stops starting. A heartbeat check answers that objection. For alert delivery, a polling consumer can examine recent unresolved groups and maintain its own notification state so one group does not trigger a newly introduced message on every poll. Treat this as an operational component with an owner, not as an incidental catch block.

    #92158. Latest Update: The page that reads easily gets believed. Fluency is doing more selling than your accuracy claim.

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (557 w)
    📖 Baca

    Latest Update: The page that reads easily gets believed. Fluency is doing more selling than your accuracy claim.

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (557 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dev

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that two data files, identical rows, identical source.
    • When something is easy to read, the brain treats the ease as evidence.
    • My first product page was a monument of effort.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that two data files, identical rows, identical source. One is described in a wall of bold headers, exclamation marks and a fifteen-point feature list. The other is described in four plain sentences and one date. Buyers rate the second one as more accurate. Not more attractive. More accurate.

    That is processing fluency at work. When something is easy to read, the brain treats the ease as evidence. It does not say "this was easy to read". It says "this feels right", and then it invents a reason: the data must be well organised.

    I learned this the expensive way. My first product page was a monument of effort. Thirty-one field names. Every county. A paragraph on deduplication logic. I was proud of it and it converted at nothing, because a buyer scrolling on a phone at 11pm does not read thirty-one field names. He reads the first line to see if this is someone like him, then he skims for a number that proves work was done, then he looks for the price and the exit.

    What I changed, and what I would tell anyone selling a file:.

    Sources indicate that say what it is in one sentence a tired person can repeat. "Every care location registered with the CQC in England, 57,191 rows, rebuilt from their own monthly export." Then one number that could only come from real work. Then the date. Then the price. Everything else belongs below, for the man who has already decided and now wants to check your homework.

    In a recent development, second thing: shorten the words. "Deduplicated" became "one row per location". "Canonicalised postcode field" became "postcodes are full, not the first four characters". Every technical term is a small tax on belief, and buyers who do not pay it never reach your price.

    Third: one decision per screen. My page used to ask him to pick a plan, add a discount, and choose a format before he had understood what he was buying. Three decisions is a survey. One decision is a purchase.

    The uncomfortable part: fluency makes a worse file sound better than a good one. That means a genuinely rigorous dataset sold in dense language loses to a sloppy one sold in plain language. This is not fair and it is not changing. The correct response is not to make your data vague, it is to make the honest version easy: plain sentences, one number, one date, and the boring truth about what is missing, written short enough that he actually reads it.

    Test it cheaply. Send your page to someone who does not work in your field and ask what they think you are selling and how much it costs. If they hesitate, the buyer will too, and the buyer will not ask you to clarify. He will just leave and buy nothing, and your analytics will call it a bounce.

    In a recent development, ease of reading is not decoration. It is the cheapest accuracy claim you own, and it is the only one the buyer can verify in three seconds without doing work.

    Industry observers note that I rebuild these datasets from the official registries every week (UK CQC care providers, SEC Form D, US city permits, HHS OIG exclusions). Free 50-row sample before you pay: https://kailou4.gumroad.com.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Imagine a world in which you can do transactions and many other things without having to give your personal information.
    • According to recent reports, it’s like your computer’s hard drive.
    • Blockchain technology was originally invented in 1991 by two mathematicians, Stuart Haber and W.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Imagine a world in which you can do transactions and many other things without having to give your personal information. A world in which you don’t need to rely on banks or governments anymore. Sounds amazing, right? That’s exactly what blockchain technology allows us to do.

    According to recent reports, it’s like your computer’s hard drive. blockchain is a technology that lets you store data in digital blocks, which are connected together like links in a chain.

    Blockchain technology was originally invented in 1991 by two mathematicians, Stuart Haber and W. Scot Stornetta. They first proposed the system to ensure that timestamps could not be tampered with.

    A few years later, in 1998, software developer Nick Szabo proposed using a similar kind of technology to secure a digital payments system he called “Bit Gold.” However, this innovation was not adopted until Satoshi Nakamoto claimed to have invented the first Blockchain and Bitcoin.

    A blockchain is a distributed database shared between the nodes of a computer network. It saves information in digital format. Many people first heard of blockchain technology when they started to look up information about bitcoin.

    Blockchain is used in cryptocurrency systems to ensure secure, decentralized records of transactions.

    Blockchain allowed people to guarantee the fidelity and security of a record of data without the need for a third party to ensure accuracy.

    To understand how a blockchain works, Consider these basic steps:.

    Let’s get to know more about the blockchain.

    Sources indicate that blockchain records digital information and distributes it across the network without changing it. The information is distributed among many users and stored in an immutable, permanent ledger that can't be changed or destroyed. That's why blockchain is also called "Distributed Ledger Technology" or DLT.

    According to recent reports, and that’s the beauty of it! The process may seem complicated, but it’s done in minutes with modern technology. And because technology is advancing rapidly, I expect things to move even more quickly than ever.

    According to recent reports, even though blockchain is integral to cryptocurrency, it has other applications. For example, blockchain can be used for storing reliable data about transactions. Many people confuse blockchain with cryptocurrencies like bitcoin and ethereum.

    Recent findings suggest that blockchain already being adopted by some massive-name companies, such as Walmart, AIG, Siemens, Pfizer, and Unilever. For example, IBM's Food Trust uses blockchain to track food's journey before reaching its final destination.

    It has been revealed that although some of you may consider this practice excessive, food suppliers and manufacturers adhere to the policy of tracing their products because bacteria such as E. coli and Salmonella have been found in packaged foods. In addition, there have been isolated cases where dangerous allergens such as peanuts have accidentally been introduced into certain products.

    It has been revealed that tracing and identifying the sources of an outbreak is a challenging task that can take months or years. Thanks to the Blockchain, however, companies now know exactly where their food has been—so they can trace its location and prevent future outbreaks.

    Blockchain technology allows systems to react much faster in the event of a hazard. It also has many other uses in the modern world.

    Sources indicate that blockchain technology is safe, even if it’s public. People can access the technology using an internet connection.

    It has been revealed that have you ever been in a situation where you had all your data stored at one place and that one secure place got compromised? Wouldn't it be great if there was a way to prevent your data from leaking out even when the security of your storage systems is compromised?

    Blockchain technology provides a way of avoiding this situation by using multiple computers at different locations to store information about transactions. If one computer experiences problems with a transaction, it will not affect the other nodes.

    According to recent reports, instead, other nodes will use the correct information to cross-reference your incorrect node. This is called “Decentralization,” meaning all the information is stored in multiple places.

    Blockchain guarantees your data's authenticity—not just its accuracy, but also its irreversibility. It can also be used to store data that are difficult to register, like legal contracts, state identifications, or a company's product inventory.

    Blockchain has many advantages and disadvantages.

    I’ll answer the most frequently asked questions about blockchain in this section.

    Sources indicate that blockchain is not a cryptocurrency but a technology that makes cryptocurrencies possible. It's a digital ledger that records every transaction seamlessly.

    Yes, blockchain can be theoretically hacked, but it is a complicated task to be achieved. A network of people constantly reviews it, which makes hacking the blockchain difficult.

    Coinbase Global is at the moment the biggest blockchain company in the world. The company runs a commendable infrastructure, services, and technology for the digital currency economy.

    In a recent development, blockchain is a decentralized technology. It’s a chain of distributed ledgers connected with nodes. Each node can be any electronic device. Thus, one owns blockhain.

    Bitcoin is a cryptocurrency, which is powered by Blockchain technology while Blockchain is a distributed ledger of cryptocurrency.

    According to recent reports, generally a database is a collection of data which can be stored and organized using a database management system. The people who have access to the database can view or edit the information stored there. The client-server network architecture is used to implement databases. whereas a blockchain is a growing list of records, called blocks, stored in a distributed system. Each block contains a cryptographic hash of the previous block, timestamp and transaction information. Modification of data is not allowed due to the design of the blockchain. The technology allows decentralized control and eliminates risks of data modification by other parties.

    Blockchain has a wide spectrum of applications and, over the next 5-10 years, we will likely see it being integrated into all sorts of industries. From finance to healthcare, blockchain could revolutionize the way we store and share data. Although there is some hesitation to adopt blockchain systems right now, that won't be the case in 2022-2023 (and even less so in 2026). Once people become more comfortable with the technology and understand how it can work for them, owners, CEOs and entrepreneurs alike will be quick to leverage blockchain technology for their own gain.     📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, affiliate marketing is a way to make money by promoting the products and services of other people and companies. You don't need to create your product or service, just promote existing ones. That's why it's so easy to get started with affiliate marketing. You can even get started with no budget at all!

    An affiliate program is a package of information you create for your product, which is then made available to potential publishers. The program will typically include details about the product and its retail value, commission levels, and promotional materials. Many affiliate programs are managed via an affiliate network like ShareASale, which acts as a platform to connect publishers and advertisers, but it is also possible to offer your program directly.

    In a recent development, affiliate networks connect publishers to advertisers. Affiliate networks make money by charging fees to the merchants who advertise with them; these merchants are known as advertisers. The percentage of each sale that the advertiser pays is negotiated between the merchant and the affiliate network.

    Dropshipping is a method of selling that allows you to run an online store without having to stock products. You advertise the products as if you owned them, but when someone makes an order, you create a duplicate order with the distributor at a reduced price. The distributor takes care of the post and packaging on your behalf. As affiliate marketing is based on referrals and this type of drop shipping requires no investment in inventory when a customer buys through the affiliate link, no money exchanges hands.

    Recent findings suggest that performance marketing is a method of marketing that pays for performance, like when a sale is made or an ad is clicked This can include methods like PPC (pay-per-click) or display advertising. Affiliate marketing is one form of performance marketing where commissions are paid out to affiliates on a performance basis when they click on their affiliate link and make a purchase or action.

    Recent findings suggest that smartphones are essentially miniature computers, so publishers can display the same websites and offers that are available on a PC. But mobiles also offer specific tools not available on computers, and these can be used to good effect for publishers. Publishers can optimize their ads for mobile people by making them easy to access by this audience. Publishers can also make good use of text and instant messaging to promote their offers. As the mobile market is predicted to make up 80% of traffic in the future, publishers who do not promote on mobile devices are missing out on a massive opportunity.

    Recent findings suggest that the best way to find affiliate publishers is on reputable networks like ShareASale Cj(Commission Junction), Awin, and Impact radius. These networks have a strict application process and compliance checks, which means that all affiliates are trustworthy.

    An affiliate disclosure statement discloses to the reader that there may be affiliate links on a website, for which a commission may be paid to the publisher if visitors follow these links and make purchases.

    It has been revealed that publishers promote their programs through a variety of means, including blogs, websites, email marketing, and pay-per-click ads. Social media has a huge interactive audience, making this platform a good source of potential traffic.

    Recent findings suggest that A super affiliate is an affiliate partner who consistently drives a large majority of sales from any program they promote, compared to other affiliate partners involved in that program. Affiliates make a lot of money from affiliate marketing Pat Flynn earned more than $50000 in 2013 from affiliate marketing.

    According to recent reports, because the Internet is so widespread, affiliate programs can be promoted in any country. Affiliate strategies that are set internationally need to be tailored to the language of the targeted country.

    Affiliate marketing can help you grow your business in the following ways:.

    It has been revealed that one of the best ways to work with qualified affiliates is to hire an affiliate marketing agency that works with all the networks. Affiliates are carefully selected and go through a rigorous application process to be included in the network.

    Affiliate marketing is generally associated with websites, but there are other ways to promote your affiliate links, including:.

    Commission rates are typically based on a percentage of the total sale and in some cases can also be a flat fee for each transaction. The rates are set by the merchant.

    Who manages your affiliate program?

    Some merchants run their affiliate programs internally, while others choose to contract out management to a network or an external agency.

    • Industry observers note that if you’re late to the AI party, don’t worry.
    • Personalize is an AI-powered technology that helps you identify and produce highly targeted sales and marketing campaigns by tracking the products and services your contacts are most interested in at any given time.
    • Seventh Sense provides behavioral analytics that helps you win attention in your customers’ overcrowded email inboxes.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that if you’re late to the AI party, don’t worry. It’s easier than you think to start leveraging artificial intelligence tools in your marketing strategy. Here are 11 AI marketing tools every marketer should start using today.

    Personalize is an AI-powered technology that helps you identify and produce highly targeted sales and marketing campaigns by tracking the products and services your contacts are most interested in at any given time. The platform uses an algorithm to identify each contact’s top three interests, which are updated in real-time based on recent site activity.

    Seventh Sense provides behavioral analytics that helps you win attention in your customers’ overcrowded email inboxes. Choosing the best day and time to send an email is always a gamble. And while some days of the week generally get higher open rates than others, you’ll never be able to nail down a time that’s best for every customer. Seventh Sense eases your stress of having to figure out the perfect send-time and day for your email campaigns. The AI-based platform figures out the best timing and email frequency for each contact based on when they’re opening emails. The tool is primarily geared toward HubSpot and Marketo customers.

    Phrasee uses artificial intelligence to help you write more effective subject lines. With its AI-based Natural Language Generation system, Phrasee uses data-driven insights to generate millions of natural-sounding copy variants that match your brand voice. The model is end-to-end, meaning when you feed the results back to Phrasee, the prediction model rebuilds so it can continuously learn from your audience.

    Recent findings suggest that hubSpot Search Engine Optimization (SEO) is an integral tool for the Human Content team. It uses machine learning to determine how search engines understand and categorize your content. HubSpot SEO helps you improve your search engine rankings and outrank your competitors. Search engines reward websites that organize their content around core subjects, or topic clusters. HubSpot SEO helps you discover and rank for the topics that matter to your business and customers.

    When you’re limited to testing two variables against each other at a time, it can take months to get the results you’re looking for. Evolv AI lets you test all your ideas at once. It uses advanced algorithms to identify the top-performing concepts, combine them with each other, and repeat the process to achieve the best site experience.

    In a recent development, acrolinx is a content alignment platform that helps brands scale and improves the quality of their content. It’s geared toward enterprises – its major customers include substantial brands like Google, Adobe, and Amazon - to help them scale their writing efforts. Instead of spending time chasing down and fixing typos in multiple places throughout an article or blog post, you can use Acrolinx to do it all right there in one place. You start by setting your preferences for style, grammar, tone of voice, and firm-specific word usage. Then, Acrolinx checks and scores your existing content to find what’s working and suggest areas for improvement. The platform provides real-time guidance and suggestions to make writing better and strengthen weak pages.

    MarketMuse uses an algorithm to help marketers build content strategies. The tool reveals you where to target keywords to rank in specific topic categories, and recommends keywords you should go after if you want to own particular topics. It also identifies gaps and opportunities for latest content and prioritizes them by their probable impact on your rankings. The algorithm compares your content with thousands of articles related to the same topic to uncover what’s missing from your site.

    Copilot is a suite of tools that help eCommerce businesses maintain real-time communication with customers around the clock at every stage of the funnel. Promote products, recover shopping carts and send updates or reminders directly through Messenger.

    According to recent reports, yotpo’s deep learning technology evaluates your customers’ product reviews to help you make better business decisions. It identifies key topics that customers mention related to your products—and their feelings toward them. The AI engine extracts relevant reviews from past buyers and presents them in smart displays to convert new shoppers. Yotpo also saves you time moderating reviews. The AI-powered moderation tool automatically assigns a score to each review and flags reviews with negative sentiment so you can focus on quality control instead of manually reviewing every post.

    Recent findings suggest that albert is a self-learning software that automates the creation of marketing campaigns for your brand. It analyzes vast amounts of data to run optimized campaigns autonomously, allowing you to feed in your own creative content and target markets, and then use data from its database to determine key characteristics of a serious buyer. Albert identifies potential customers that match those traits, and runs trial campaigns on a small group of customers—with results refined by Albert himself—before launching it on a larger scale.

    Recent findings suggest that albert plugs into your existing marketing technology stack, so you still have access to your accounts, ads, search, social media, and more. Albert maps tracking and attribution to your source of truth so you can determine which channels are driving your business.

    Industry observers note that there are many tools and companies out there that offer AI tools, but this is a small list of resources that we have found to be helpful. If you have any other suggestions, feel free to share them in the comments below this article. As marketing evolves at such a rapid pace, new marketing strategies will be invented that we haven't even dreamed of yet. But for now, this list should give you a good starting point on your way to implementing AI into your marketing mix.
