    #92113. The 9 Best Chain Restaurant BLTs, According To Customer Reviews

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (2033 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    The 9 Best Chain Restaurant BLTs, According To Customer Reviews

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2033 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A good BLT is elegantly simple, a masterclass in culinary economy.
    • These details make it hard for chain restaurants to nail a great BLT.
    • Cook Out has built a restaurant empire on selling comfort foods that you'd find at a backyard barbecue.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A good BLT is elegantly simple, a masterclass in culinary economy. With this sandwich, nothing is superfluous, nothing is forced. Instead, each ingredient works in unison to create an unmatched harmony of taste, temperature, and texture. Whether you're craving a light nosh or a substantial sit-down lunch, somehow a BLT always fits the bill. And because of its pared-down composition, every element has a chance to shine on its own. However, this also means there's no place to hide mistakes. If the tomato is a bit mealy, the bacon slightly chewy, or the bread a tad soft, it can throw off the entire sandwich.

    These details make it hard for chain restaurants to nail a great BLT. They serve thousands of meals every day, and each individual order exposes them to a world of criticism and critique. To save yourself from a sub-par sandwich, you need to know which chains are executing a quality BLT. And this list hopes to do just that, featuring a handful of fast food chains and restaurants that are dishing up both familiar renditions and inventive interpretations of this classic sandwich. To find the best, I searched social media, roundups, and other online forums to uncover which chain restaurants are doing the BLT justice.

    Cook Out has built a restaurant empire on selling comfort foods that you'd find at a backyard barbecue. From hush puppies to corn dogs to some of the best fast food milkshakes in the country. But it also offers a fun take on the classic BLT. While most people judge the sandwich's quality by the crispness of its lettuce, the juiciness of its tomato, or the number of grains in its whole wheat bread, Cook Out takes a different approach: speed, price, and efficiency.

    It has been revealed that these sandwiches are essentially BLT sliders: compact handhelds you can devour rapidly and without a tummy ache. Despite their size, photos show you get a decent amount of each ingredient packed onto the tiny hamburger bun. And at a time when value is a particularly tasty quality, the fact that these mini sandwiches cost between $2 and $3.49 (depending on your location) makes them even more delicious. "They are ridiculously cheap," said one customer on Facebook. "Less than two bucks..." On Reddit, the feelings are mutual, with another commenter posting, "The BLTs are the unsung hero of Cook Out." Apparently, not all heroes wear capes; some wear bacon.

    Industry observers note that sonic is another chain known for its nostalgic, carhop-inspired food. It has all the munchies you crave late at night: tater tots, root beer floats, breakfast burritos — really, the menu covers the gamut. But the restaurant is best known for its selection of classics, including the BLT. While some BLTs are light and dainty, Sonic's BLT Toaster is on the heftier side, perfect if you're craving something not greasy but still substantial enough to keep you full throughout the day. The sandwich isn't such a departure from classic BLTs, but everything just feels, well, bigger. The hand-sliced tomatoes, fresh lettuce, and trio of meaty bacon strips all come sandwiched between two thick slabs of buttery Texas toast.

    Customers, say that they love the BLT, with one YouTuber noting it's "crispy, crunchy, and yummy." And speaking of breakfast, Sonic's BLT Toaster is frustratingly elusive. It's not discontinued, but it doesn't always appear when ordering online. A workaround is to get the Grilled Cheese and just add bacon, lettuce, and tomato. Or you can just ask for it specifically if ordering in person.

    Potbelly knows how to put together a quality sandwich, and as far as chain sub shops go, it should be in the conversation with Jersey Mike's, Jimmy John's, and Firehouse Subs — at least that's what people are saying on the Reddit threads. However, like most fast food empires, quality varies by location. Still, a good Potbelly sandwich is as solid as any, typically well-stuffed, with a great ratio of condiments and toppings.

    This same formula and attention to detail that make its Italian sub a customer favorite also show up in its BLTA (the "A" stands for avocado). Texturally, it's a terrific blend of creamy, cool, crispy, and crunchy, and unlike the more value-friendly fast food restaurants, the sandwich is assembled with a little more care. Customers note that the avocado is freshly sliced, the bread is crusty and substantial, and the pepper-crusted, applewood-smoked bacon is the best of any sandwich chain. "Potbelly makes an amazing BLT," claims one happy diner on Instagram. "...the lettuce and tomato are fresh and refreshing. The bacon is peppered, which adds a great flavor. The bread-to-ingredients ratio is amazing. Solid BLT 9/10.".

    Jason's Deli is more than just a deli. It has more than 200 locations, mostly in the South and Midwest, which is why it probably doesn't get the national acclaim it deserves. But Jason's makes some incredible food that's unlike anything else you'll find at other fast food restaurants and casual chains: giant baked potatoes, massive slow-cooked brisket sandwiches, and a bottomless salad bar that might just be the best in the country.

    Its version of a BLT — aptly named the Bigger Better BLT — is no slouch, either, although it's sure to ruffle the feathers of BLT purists. Why? Well, the sandwich is stuffed with a few extra letters from the alphabet. Obviously, it includes the standard bacon, lettuce, and tomato — albeit in greater quantity than average —plus slices of avocado and a freshly cracked fried egg, all piled on two slices of multi-grain wheat. In general, customers are impressed by the amount of bacon and the overall sandwich composition. "This is my favorite menu item from here," stated a Redditor after posting a glam shot of their sandwich.

    According to recent reports, from its famous #13 Original Italian to the Big Kahuna Cheesesteak, Jersey Mike's knows how to put together a sandwich. The chain takes the same thoughtful approach with its #1 BLT. Our sister site, Chowhound, ranked it the tastiest chain restaurant BLT around, citing the quantity of ingredients and textural harmony as key reasons for its success.

    Jersey Mike's doesn't do anything special with its BLT. No bells and whistles or novel additions; it just nails the basics, with a precise ratio of tender tomato, refreshing shredded lettuce, crispy bacon, and a good mayonnaise (and some oil and vinegar or chopped pepper relish if you get it "Mike's Way"). The bread cradles the ingredients so nothing gets too soggy or, worse, falls apart.

    On a Facebook post dedicated to the BLT debate, one person commented, "Jersey Mike's is the only place I will go for 'fast food' subs!" Others agree, with another poster noting, "...this was wayyyy good [...] I only wish I got extra bacon, but there was a good amount." And while everyone appreciates a simple sandwich, many customers say their customizations improve the taste, adding everything from tangy banana peppers to spicy chipotle mayo to your standard slice of American cheese.

    Sources indicate that five Guys is known for its juicy burgers, thick milkshakes, and an unnecessary abundance of fries, but the fast food restaurant also makes one of the best BLTs of any national chain. However, Five Guys created some confusion among its fan base by formally "launching" the BLT sandwich just a few months ago, even though many loyal customers say it's more of a relaunch, given that it's been available for more than a decade.

    Regardless, the sandwich is now available nationwide, which is good news for anyone who loves a BLT that doesn't skimp on the B. The sandwich is served on a sesame seed burger bun, but the applewood-smoked bacon is piled so high that it's about the thickness of a double (or triple) stacked cheeseburger. "They PILE the bacon on those BLTs," commented one Redditor, "...it's unlike any BLT I've ever had because of the sheer volume of meat." Facebook owners have similar feelings. Overall, customers view it as an underappreciated alternative to the major sandwich chains, especially for the price, which is a few dollars less than Five Guys' standard burger. On a Facebook post comparing BLTs from other chains, one person commented: "Should have gone to Five Guys. That's the GOAT BLT.".

    In a recent development, cheba Hut has been around since 1998, with its original location satisfying hungry students from the Arizona State University campus. Its menu reflects the playful, somewhat frenzied, college-kid mentality. Sandwiches are bold and inventive, with names and ingredient combinations that would make Panera Bread blush. Its version of the BLT — the Sensi Kush — has a traditional foundation of bacon, lettuce, and tomato, but it also includes a few, dare we say, dank touches that set it apart from your other basic sandwich chain, specifically a drizzle of sriracha honey, fresh avocado, and a buttery blanket of provolone.

    According to recent reports, is this genius or BLT blasphemy? Based on customer reviews, it is most definitely the former. "I love a good BLT but I really love the Sensi Kush BLT from Cheba Hut! The honey sriracha sauce is 100," noted one Facebook user, along with a pic of their sandwich. Customers on Instagram agree, with one commenter writing, "The sensi kush is fire," while another on Reddit said, "I love Cheba Hut! I think they make the best BLT I've ever had.".

    According to recent reports, first Watch is a sizable chain with nearly 700 locations across mostly the eastern half of the United States. The restaurant offers a diverse lineup that emphasizes freshness and ingredient quality over speed and cost. At First Watch, there's something for everyone: lemon ricotta pancakes, power breakfast bowls, Benedicts, elaborate, lunch-y salads, etc., but when it comes to sandwiches, its BLT(E) is one of the best.

    It pairs your typical BLT with two over-hard eggs (can't have messy yolks getting everything soggy) and Monterey Jack cheese — all on its artisan whole-grain bread. BLT snobs may scoff at the extra ingredients, but the bread, along with the sandwich's overall engineering, is as good as you'll find at a local cafe or diner. The portion is sizable, bordering on two portions-worth. The sandwich's flavor takes people by surprise as well, with it being filling and tasty while not weighing you down. One Instagram post noted, "I enjoyed the BLTE [...]. It was so good. [...] I think I might start orderind sandwiches at First Watch each time I go." For something even more out there, try First Watch's BLT Benedict, which is basically an open-faced BLT sandwich topped with poached eggs and hollandaise.

    Recent findings suggest that celebrity endorsements don't mean everything, but John Oliver (the star of HBO's Last Week Tonight) once publicly stated to his friend Stephen Colbert that his favorite sandwich is none other than a Wawa BLT. But this shouldn't be such a shock. Wawa is famous for its reasonably priced subs and sandwiches, and its BLT doesn't disappoint (at least when the bacon is properly cooked). While a Tasting Table ranking didn't put the BLT at the top of the list, the author still praised the sandwich, saying it was "perfectly built...nicely slathered with creamy mayo and stuffed with strips of bacon, shredded lettuce, and sliced tomato.".

    In a recent development, some chains (even a few on this list) are guilty of — every so often — skimping on ingredients. Not Wawa. Its sandwiches are pretty stuffed. One Facebook user said, "The BLT hyperfixation is in fullllllll effect." Even if you do end up with a thin sandwich, the staff will gladly remake it to your liking. Another ordering tip: Wawa recently moved the BLT from the "cold" to "hot" sandwich section, which has caused some confusion amongst customers over fears that it had been discontinued.

    To find the chain restaurants with the best BLTs that delivered on taste, price, and overall value, we dug through dozens of online forums, social media video reviews, and taste tests from within the past year. In the end, this list represents some of the best BLTs you can find, based on photos, reviews, and customer feedback.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

    Sources indicate that A classic grilled cheese is a thing of both beauty and comfort. And of course, a simple sandwich such as this is open to interpretation, with many putting their own spin on it, like making it Swiss-style with raclette cheese or switching up the grilling process by using an air fryer, like Ree Drummond. But there's an easy addition you can make to your next grilled cheese that will make it even tastier (and it's not mayo or butter, though you can certainly use either): It's store-bought caramelized onion dip.

    Sources indicate that when spread onto the bread and covered in cheese, then warmed through in a hot pan, caramelized onion dip brings a burst of flavor and a compelling texture to the sandwich. Of course, it's definitely savory, but the caramelized onions also introduce a subtly sweet element to grilled cheese, creating a flavor sensation that is much more interesting for your taste buds. Meanwhile, the dip melts into the cheese, adding to the creaminess, while the onions introduce a little toothsome variety to chew on, beyond the softness of the filling and the crispness of the bread.

    In a recent development, trader Joe's Caramelized Onion Dip is one great store-bought option, and it's part of the store's regular lineup, so you should be able to find it year-round (unless it has sold out). Whole Foods also sells a version under its 365 brand, which Amazon Prime members can shop for on Amazon.

    If you have the desire to take things a step further, you might try a mix-in or two that can elevate the taste of the dip (and therefore, your entire sandwich). That might include some dried cranberries, which can help draw out the aforementioned sweetness of the onions, creating an even bolder contrast in your salty grilled cheese. You also might play to the richness and crumble up some crisp bacon into the base. Or enhance the savory, aromatic vibes by adding both thinly sliced scallions and chives.

    Now, if you're having trouble finding caramelized onion dip at your grocery store, you could always make your own, though cooking down the onions properly can be laborious. If standing over your stove for 45 minutes doesn't appeal to you, Ina Garten cuts down on the time by using a larger pot, which allows the onions to cook more evenly and efficiently. But if you'd rather skip the cooking altogether, you might find the adjacent caramelized onion jam on store shelves. This won't be as creamy as the dip, but it will still impart that same rich, savory, and slightly sweet flavor, so it's a decent substitution.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that incorporating secret ingredients into your burger patties elevates the dish in unexpected ways.
    • Industry observers note that yogurt's contained lactic acid functions as a mild, but nevertheless efficient, tenderizer, lightly marinating the meat.
    • Recent findings suggest that and if you use Greek yogurt for the task, you'll get a nice dose of added protein, too.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that incorporating secret ingredients into your burger patties elevates the dish in unexpected ways. Some components flavor the meat while others enhance the texture. For an add-in that does both — with a delicious underlying creaminess — look no further than yogurt. The dairy works as a ground beef tenderizer, making a burger that's softer and full of moisture. Not to mention, yogurt is an effective enhancement in chicken or turkey patties, too.

    Industry observers note that yogurt's contained lactic acid functions as a mild, but nevertheless efficient, tenderizer, lightly marinating the meat. The inclusion of a liquid naturally adds lots of moisture to a burger — you certainly won't have to worry about a disappointingly dry result. Plus, the ingredient lends the burger a lightly creamy mouthfeel.

    Recent findings suggest that and if you use Greek yogurt for the task, you'll get a nice dose of added protein, too. Mix in a quarter cup of whole milk Greek yogurt — a quantity suitable for a pound of meat — and you'll up the dish by 5.5 grams of protein. This yogurt's extra fat content will further prevent dryness, all while forming a patty that's not too loose, making a burger rendition that stands out.

    Working yogurt into your beef patties doesn't require any special technique. You can simply stir the dairy with the beef in a bowl, seasoning with salt and pepper in parallel. Follow by forming the patties as usual, then lightly brush the exterior with oil to prevent unwanted adhesion. Prepare the yogurt burgers using your preferred method, whether you're fond of using a skillet or grilling burgers like a pro. However, if you notice your mixture appears too wet, consider adding a binder — chia seeds are a fantastic option to absorb moisture but keep things tender and juicy; panko breadcrumbs will also absorb excess liquid while keeping the bite of each burger soft.

    It has been revealed that such a burger tastes delicious with classic seasonings, but don't rule out creative modifications, too. The pairing of yogurt and beef recalls Greek and Middle Eastern cuisine, so consider integrating Eastern Mediterranean seasonings into the build.

    It has been revealed that A Greek burger spin could fold in oregano, lemon, and feta — core flavors of a Greek salad. A kofta-style patty might up the spice, working in earthy cumin, a dash of spicy harissa, and grated garlic into the mix. Alternatively, season the meat in a sweet direction by using simply turmeric and onions; the ingredients will set you up for a wide array of flavorful condiments. Build out the meal with an aromatic herbal yogurt sauce, a bold dose of roasted peppers, or a marinated arugula salad, and you'll make a burger rendition that'll become a frequent part of the rotation.

    • A simple breakfast addition improved reaction times, but its effects on memory took a more complicated turn.
    • Adding walnuts to breakfast could help people respond faster on mental tasks and learn information more effectively later in the day.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A simple breakfast addition improved reaction times, but its effects on memory took a more complicated turn.

    A simple breakfast addition improved reaction times, but its effects on memory took a more complicated turn.

    Adding walnuts to breakfast could help people respond faster on mental tasks and learn information more effectively later in the day.

    A generous handful produced small cognitive benefits over the following six hours, although memory performance varied with the timing of the tests.

    Walnuts may influence how the brain directs attention and obtains the energy needed for demanding mental work.

    Professor Claire Williams, study co-author, said:.

    “A handful of walnuts with breakfast could give young adults a mental edge when they need to perform at the top of their game.”.

    The research involved over 30 healthy young adults aged 18–30, who ate two different breakfasts on separate visits to the laboratory.

    One contained 50 g of crushed walnuts mixed into muesli and vanilla yoghurt, while the other contained no nuts.

    The breakfasts contained almost identical calorie and fat totals, with butter added to the comparison meal to help achieve this match.

    Participants completed tests before breakfast and again two, four and six hours afterwards, while researchers also recorded their brain activity.

    After the walnut breakfast, participants responded faster on tasks involving attention, resisting distractions and switching between different mental rules.

    These abilities form part of executive function, which helps us control our responses and adapt to changing demands.

    The differences were modest, averaging around eight milliseconds on the attention test and 22 milliseconds when switching between rules.

    Whether improvements of this size would make a noticeable difference outside the laboratory remains uncertain.

    The memory findings were more complicated.

    Two hours after eating walnuts, participants performed slightly worse when repeatedly learning and recalling a list of words.

    By six hours, however, the pattern had reversed, with better performance after walnuts than after the comparison breakfast.

    One possibility is that walnuts helped protect learning performance as the testing day wore on.

    Repeated mental effort can make it harder to take in upcoming information, so preserving the ability to learn could be useful even without improving every aspect of memory.

    However, participants did not report feeling less mentally fatigued after walnuts, leaving this explanation unconfirmed.

    Another possibility is that some benefits emerged gradually as nutrients were absorbed and processed.

    Walnuts contain omega-3 fats, protein and plant compounds called polyphenols, which could contribute individually or together.

    Electrical recordings revealed differences in frontal and parietal brain activity after the two breakfasts.

    These regions contribute to attention, memory and the control of behaviour.

    The changes may indicate that walnuts altered how mental resources were allocated during the tests, although they do not establish precisely why performance improved.

    Blood samples also highlighted slightly higher glucose availability and lower concentrations of circulating free fatty acids after walnuts.

    Greater glucose availability might help fuel demanding mental work.

    The study was published in the journal Food & Function (Bell et al., 2025).

    #92095. Give Canned Baked Beans A Delicious Upgrade With A Drizzle Of This Ingredient (Hint: It's Not Honey)

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (490 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    Give Canned Baked Beans A Delicious Upgrade With A Drizzle Of This Ingredient (Hint: It's Not Honey)

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (490 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • When you need a side to go along with your main dinner entree and you need one fast, it's reassuring to know that shelf-stable, pantry-sitting canned goods have got your back.
    • It has been revealed that molasses might not be the first thing you think of when you consider add-ins, but many homemade recipes call for it, and for good reason.
    • It is for this reason that molasses is also preferable to honey here.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    When you need a side to go along with your main dinner entree and you need one fast, it's reassuring to know that shelf-stable, pantry-sitting canned goods have got your back. Included in Food Republic's list of inexpensive canned foods you'll use all the time are beans, and along with the plain black or red varieties (which typically need to be combined with other ingredients to make a reasonable side), you could also reach for scrumptious, creamy baked beans. But while they're totally fine heated up straight from the can, they can certainly benefit from a drizzle of molasses.

    It has been revealed that molasses might not be the first thing you think of when you consider add-ins, but many homemade recipes call for it, and for good reason. Made by boiling down sugarcane juice or refining sugar, the rich, thick syrup is slightly smoky and sweet, with robust, burnt caramel notes, making it a perfect match for deepening the flavor of sometimes weak-tasting canned baked beans and bringing them closer to homemade.

    It is for this reason that molasses is also preferable to honey here. Honey is intensely sweet, can taste almost floral at times, and has a delicate flavor, whereas molasses is bolder and has a meatier taste that can make its presence known among the other ingredients in the dish.

    It's key to note that there are three main types of molasses: light, dark, and blackstrap, and they each have different flavor profiles. For canned baked beans, you'll likely want to stick with light or dark because blackstrap is intensely bitter (also, light is the sweetest of the three, so if sweetness is important to you, go with that one). If you're heating the beans on the stove, you can start by drizzling in about half a tablespoon of molasses per 28-ounce can, bringing the mixture to a boil, and then simmering for about 10 minutes. If you're baking them, likewise, just stir in the molasses before putting the dish in the oven — it couldn't be simpler.

    Sources indicate that if you don't have any molasses sitting about, don't panic. There are plenty of other additions that can help upgrade canned baked beans and make them taste less, well, pantry-fied. Take brown sugar, for example — did you know that it's often just white sugar and molasses combined? A little bit will still bring that sweet contrast to balance out the savory flavors and give you a deeper, more complex finish.

    Another great option is one you might normally use on your pancakes: maple syrup. You don't want to use the fake stuff that's primarily made of corn syrup and artificial flavors and colors, but rather 100% real Grade A maple syrup for the best flavor. Its sweetness again deliciously contrasts with and enhances the canned baked beans' savoriness, while the maple flavor adds its unique caramelly, toffee-like notes to the dish.

    Make Your Next Breakfast Sandwich Korean-Style For A Major Fiber & Flavor Boost

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (493 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
    • In a recent development, think of Korean cuisine, and a sandwich likely isn't the first thing that comes to mind.
    • Easy-to-make, packed with fiber, and delicious, the dish is a great candidate for your breakfast rotation.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

    In a recent development, think of Korean cuisine, and a sandwich likely isn't the first thing that comes to mind. However, bread-based dishes are widely enjoyed in the East Asian country, both in cafes and as street food. An especially popular breakfast rendition is gilgeori toast, a comforting breakfast sandwich stuffed with eggs and shredded vegetables.

    Easy-to-make, packed with fiber, and delicious, the dish is a great candidate for your breakfast rotation. Traditionally, this sandwich calls for a fluffy loaf of milk or brioche bread, the buttery soft texture turning crisp on the outside once toasted. Meanwhile, the filling comprises a variable shredded vegetable medley: Cabbage traditionally forms the centerpiece, joined by carrots, onions, scallions, and often garlic chives. Mixed with egg and then pan-fried into an aesthetic golden-brown patty, the filling delectably complements the soft bread. Gilgeori is usually rounded out with a sprinkle of sugar and a drizzle of ketchup and mustard.

    In a recent development, it's an assembly that easily comes together during bleary morning hours, yet nevertheless offers a nutritious start to the day. One sandwich can pack in around six ounces of shredded cabbage, which amounts to over 4 grams of fiber. Add up the fiber from a tablespoon of carrot, two of sliced onion, and two whole green onions, and you're including another 1.5 grams. Then, add in two slices of thick-cut brioche sandwich bread, and you've got an extra 2. That's about 7.5 grams, which is around a quarter of what you need a day, already knocked out by breakfast. Mixed with the roughly 6.5 grams of protein from the egg alongside filling bread, the sandwich serves as a terrific way to start the day.

    The morning isn't always the best time to precisely reconstruct a recipe. Thankfully, gilgeori toast welcomes a wide array of reinterpretations and ingredients. Starting with the bread, feel free to swap the milk bread for sourdough, whole wheat, or even a convenient store-bought whole grain like Ezekiel or Dave's Killer. You'll lose out on some of the dish's airiness, but potentially gain extra fiber content in the process. Two slices of Dave's Killer 21 Whole Grains and Seeds contain some 8 grams of fiber, more than doubling the total of the sandwich.

    In a recent development, up the satiation further by adding on a slice of seared ham, a filling also enjoyed in Korea. And cheese is always welcome, whether American, cheddar, or fontina – Martha Stewart's go-to for breakfast sandwiches. Instead of the sugar sprinkle, lend the dish a sweet note by using jam: Raspberry or cherry jam makes a great fit. Not to mention, you can replace the ketchup and mustard with a condiment of your preference; you can buy a bottle of Gochujang Sriracha Hot Sauce online, for instance. The template of bread and shredded vegetables works with many flavors, perfect for morning enjoyment.
